# Embodied First Exam

> The first exam for code agents in the physical world. Each question is a frozen simulation scene with a goal written for a person; the answer is a program, marked by replaying it in a fresh simulator. The questions come from many benchmark suites and are sat in two modes: privileged, with the simulator open to the agent, and standard, with only the robot. A Terminal-Bench for coding agents in robotics.

## Key facts

- 1108 tasks (449 core) from 33 benchmark suites, 46 robots, 22 simulators, 5177 graded trials.
- Settings: privileged (the agent works inside the simulator); standard (real-robot rules: the agent reaches the robot only through the robot's API); standard-realtime (standard on a running clock that never stops, offered where timing matters, mostly for dynamic tasks with moving objects or opponents). Core is the leaderboard's default view: each core task once, in its default setting.
- Marking: The answer is a program, marked by replaying it in a fresh simulator (privileged) or on the live episode (standard and standard-realtime).
- Agents ranked: Antigravity + Gemini 3.8 Flash, Antigravity + Gemini 4 Argon, Claude Code + Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Code + GLM 5.3 Flash, Codex + GPT-6 Astra, dsh + DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Also run, unranked: Codex + GPT-6 Luna.
- Run it with Harbor: `harbor run -d embodied-first-exam -a <agent> -m <model>`. Code: https://github.com/mll-lab-nu/embodied-first-exam

## Suites

- BEHAVIOR-1K: Full household activities in house-scale scenes, for a mobile two-armed robot. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=behavior-1k
- RoboLab: Tabletop tasks that test language grounding, from colours and counts to relations and order. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=robolab
- RoboCasa: Everyday kitchen skills for a mobile manipulator in procedurally generated kitchens. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=robocasa
- RoboCasa365: Atomic and long composite kitchen activities from RoboCasa's 365-task suite. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=robocasa365
- RoboCasa-GR1: A Fourier GR1 humanoid with dexterous hands, picking and placing at a counter. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=robocasa-gr1
- MetaWorld+: All 50 Meta-World v3 environments for a Sawyer arm, one frozen instance each. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=metaworldplus
- VLABench: Manipulation from language: attributes, common sense and multi-step chores. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=vlabench
- HumanoidBench: Whole-body locomotion and manipulation for a Unitree H1 humanoid. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=humanoidbench
- MolmoSpaces: Zero-shot episodes in unseen houses, for a Franka FR3 and an RB-Y1 mobile robot. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=molmospaces
- KinDER: Physical reasoning for planning and control: throw, balance, sweep, scoop, pack. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=kinder
- RoboPaint: A robot arm with a brush paints the picture it is shown, stroke by stroke, from calligraphy to oils. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=robopaint
- RoboTwin 2.0: Fifty bimanual tabletop tasks for a dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=robotwin-2
- MuJoCo Playground: Quadrupeds that walk, get up and balance, and manipulation for ALOHA 2 and a Franka Panda. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=mujoco-playground
- DexToolBench: Dexterous tool use with a hammer, a marker, an eraser, a brush, a spatula or a screwdriver. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=dextoolbench
- DexJoCo: A 16-DoF Allegro hand on a Franka arm, one hand or two. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=dexjoco
- MyoSuite: Musculoskeletal hands, arms and legs, driven one muscle excitation at a time. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=myosuite
- RoboARC: Topological puzzles, ropes, chains, cloth and IKEA furniture: separate, thread, untie, fold, assemble. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=roboarc
- RoboDojo: Bimanual manipulation over five capabilities: generalization, memory, precision, long horizons, open tasks. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=robodojo
- RoboDynamicExam: Catch, strike, carry and hand over objects that move by themselves. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=pandadyn
- BiGym 2.0: Household loco-manipulation on a walking Unitree G1. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=bigym2
- YAMLab: Two I2RT YAM arms: set a pot on a cooktop, hand a mug over and hang it. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=yamlab
- LIBERO-MAX: LIBERO tasks with one change in the middle of the task. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=libero-max
- Embodied Olympics - Fun (Robo Olympics, RoboOlympics): Humanoid sports at official sizes, from sprints and jumps to dunks and backflips, judged by a referee. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=embodied-olympics-fun
- Embodied Olympics - Match (Robo Olympics, RoboOlympics): Whole matches against scripted and learned opponents: table tennis, badminton, soccer, foosball, fencing. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=embodied-olympics-match
- AM-Bench: Aerial manipulation: a flying hexarotor with an arm presses, pulls, turns and picks. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=ambench
- AutoBio: A biology bench: thermal cycler, mixer, centrifuge, screw caps and a pipette. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=autobio
- LabUtopia: A chemistry laboratory: glassware, a heater, an instrument panel, an oven and drawers. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=labutopia
- Embodied Safety Exam: Do what is harmless, refuse what would hurt someone, and say why. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=embodied-safety-exam
- DexHandExam: Five-finger hands: reorient, regrasp, fold paper, sweep and build a hamburger. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=dexhand
- iSpatialGym: The goal is a picture: make the scene look like it. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=ispatialgym
- RoboWits: Tabletop tasks that need a physical insight, like a ruler to align things or a funnel to pour. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=robowits
- ManiGuard: Manipulation safety. A task counts only if no safety rule was broken on the way. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=maniguard
- RoboEngineer: Simulate real-world sim2real engineering: train, deploy, diagnose failures, and improve. https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/suite/?id=roboengineer

## Questions

### What is the Embodied First Exam?

The first exam for code agents in the physical world. Each question is a frozen simulation scene with a goal written for a person; the answer is a program, marked by replaying it in a fresh simulator. The questions come from many benchmark suites and are sat in two modes: privileged, with the simulator open to the agent, and standard, with only the robot. A Terminal-Bench for coding agents in robotics.

### Is it a Terminal-Bench for robotics?

Yes: A Terminal-Bench for coding agents in robotics. A coding agent in its harness (such as Codex, Claude Code or Antigravity) writes a program for a robot. The answer is a program, marked by replaying it in a fresh simulator (privileged) or on the live episode (standard and standard-realtime). The exam runs through Harbor, so one command can evaluate any agent on any task.

### How do coding agents do on robots?

See the leaderboard at https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/leaderboard/ for Antigravity + Gemini 3.8 Flash, Antigravity + Gemini 4 Argon, Claude Code + Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Code + GLM 5.3 Flash, Codex + GPT-6 Astra, dsh + DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.

### What is the real-time setting?

standard-realtime: standard on a running clock that never stops, offered where timing matters, mostly for dynamic tasks with moving objects or opponents; 59 core tests.

### What are privileged and standard?

privileged: the agent works inside the simulator; standard: real-robot rules: the agent reaches the robot only through the robot's API.

### RoboLab

120 tabletop manipulation tasks for a fixed-base arm, built to test language grounding and goal specification rather than locomotion: colour and size references, counting, spatial relations, sorting, ordered stacking, reorientation. Success is a composable predicate over object state, with partial credit from scored subtasks.

Simulator: Isaac Lab 2.3.2 / Isaac Sim 5.1 (NVIDIA) · Edition: v0.3.1 (2026-08-11) · Robots: Franka + Robotiq 2F-85 · Adapted from an upstream benchmark

Tasks: Apple And Yogurt In Bowl; Banana In Bowl; Banana Then Rubiks Cube; Bananas In Bin One More; Bananas In Bin Three Total; Bananas Out Of Bin; Bbq Sauce In Bin; Block Stacking Order Agnostic; Block Stacking Specified Order; Blocks In Bin; Butter Above Raisin; Clutter Plastic; Clutter Pumpkin; Condiments In Bin; Cooking Clear Plate; Cubes And Blocks In Bin; Food Packing2 Cans; Food Packing3 Cans; Fruits Green Limes On Plate; Fruits On Plate3; Keyboard Out Of Bin; Larger Object Raisin Box In Bin; Marker In Mug; Mustard Above Raisin; Mustard In Left Bin; Mustard In Right Bin; Pick Glasses; Pick Orange Object; Pick Up Blue Pitcher; Plastic Bottles In Square Pail; Put Two Mugs On Shelf; Recycle Carton; Recycle Cartons Vertical Crate; Red Dishes In Bin; Reorient Red Mug; Rubiks Cube And Banana; Rubiks Cube Behind Bowl; Rubiks Cube In Front Of Bowl; Rubiks Cube Left Of Bowl; Rubiks Cube Right Of Bowl; Rubiks Cube Then Banana; Rubiks Cubes In Bin; Spoon In Mug; Stack Yellow On Red; Stack3 Rubiks Cube; Take Measuring Spoon Out; Take Mugs Off Of Shelf; Take Spatula Off Shelf; Throw Away Snacks; Tools Picking Drill; Unstack Rubiks Cube; Utensils In Mug; White Mug In Center Of Table.

### RoboCasa

Everyday kitchen tasks for a mobile manipulator in large procedurally generated kitchens: opening and closing doors and drawers, turning knobs and faucets, pressing buttons, and picking and placing between counters, cabinets, sinks, stoves and appliances, single- and multi-stage. We keep the 29 tasks with an official demonstration at the pinned commit whose demonstration re-verifies as a reference on a frozen instance (its first episode's initial state). Each task passes or fails on the environment's own success checker on the state after the last action, with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: full simulator state, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (standard: the robot's own four cameras, one episode, no reset).

Simulator: robosuite 1.5.1 / MuJoCo 3.2.6 (RoboCasa v0.2) · Edition: RoboCasa v0.2 @ 756598a, our selection of 29 tasks (exam @ 8c5594a43) · Robots: Franka Panda on an Omron base · Adapted from an upstream benchmark

Tasks: Multi-stage · ArrangeVegetables; Multi-stage · MicrowaveThawing; Multi-stage · PreSoakPan; Multi-stage · PrepareCoffee; Multi-stage · RestockPantry; Single-stage · CloseDoubleDoor; Single-stage · CloseDrawer; Single-stage · CloseSingleDoor; Single-stage · CoffeePressButton; Single-stage · CoffeeServeMug; Single-stage · CoffeeSetupMug; Single-stage · OpenDoubleDoor; Single-stage · OpenDrawer; Single-stage · OpenSingleDoor; Single-stage · PnPCabToCounter; Single-stage · PnPCounterToCab; Single-stage · PnPCounterToMicrowave; Single-stage · PnPCounterToSink; Single-stage · PnPCounterToStove; Single-stage · PnPMicrowaveToCounter; Single-stage · PnPSinkToCounter; Single-stage · PnPStoveToCounter; Single-stage · TurnOffMicrowave; Single-stage · TurnOffSinkFaucet; Single-stage · TurnOffStove; Single-stage · TurnOnMicrowave; Single-stage · TurnOnSinkFaucet; Single-stage · TurnOnStove; Single-stage · TurnSinkSpout.

### RoboCasa365

RoboCasa's 365-task kitchen suite for the same mobile manipulator: atomic skills and long composite activities across cooking, cleaning, storing and serving. We keep 50 of the families with a validated demonstration, chosen by a fixed rule (12 atomic, 38 composite, in SHA-256 order of their names), one frozen instance each. Each task passes or fails on the environment's own success checker on the state after the last action, with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: full simulator state, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (standard: the robot's own four cameras, one episode, no reset).

Simulator: robosuite 1.5.2 / MuJoCo 3.3.1 (RoboCasa365) · Edition: RoboCasa365 (robocasa 1.0.1 @ 4f8a298), our selection of 50 tasks (exam @ 8c5594a43) · Robots: Franka Panda on an Omron base · Adapted from an upstream benchmark

Tasks: Atomic · CloseDrawer; Atomic · CloseOven; Atomic · CloseStandMixerHead; Atomic · OpenDishwasher; Atomic · PackDessert; Atomic · PickPlaceCabinetToCounter; Atomic · PickPlaceSinkToCounter; Atomic · TurnOffMicrowave; Atomic · TurnOnMicrowave; Atomic · TurnOnSinkFaucet; Atomic · TurnOnToasterOven; Composite · AddLemonToFish; Composite · AssembleCookingArray; Composite · BeverageSorting; Composite · BreadAndCheese; Composite · CandleCleanup; Composite · CerealAndBowl; Composite · ChooseMeasuringCup; Composite · ClearFoodWaste; Composite · ClearSink; Composite · CookieDoughPrep; Composite · DeliverBrewedCoffee; Composite · DessertUpgrade; Composite · DisplayMeatVariety; Composite · DivideBasins; Composite · DrainVeggies; Composite · DrinkwareConsolidation; Composite · MakeIceLemonade; Composite · MakeLoadedPotato; Composite · MealPrepStaging; Composite · MicrowaveDefrostMeat; Composite · OrganizeCoffeeCondiments; Composite · OvenBroilFish; Composite · PlateSteakMeal; Composite · PortionInTupperware; Composite · PreRinseStation; Composite · PrepForSanitizing; Composite · PrepMarinatingMeat; Composite · ReheatMeal; Composite · RetrieveMeat; Composite · SanitizePrepCuttingBoard; Composite · ScrubBowl; Composite · SearingMeat; Composite · SeasoningSpiceSetup; Composite · SetUpCuttingStation; Composite · StockingBreakfastFoods; Composite · SweetenCoffee; Composite · ThawInSink; Composite · TongBuffetSetup; Kitchen · TurnOnStove.

### RoboCasa-GR1

A Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands at a kitchen counter: picking objects from one container or surface and placing them in another, including novel objects, and placing into a cabinet, drawer or microwave and closing it. We keep all 24 environments with an official demonstration, one frozen instance each (the demonstration's initial state). Each task passes or fails on the environment's own success checker on the state after the last action, with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: full simulator state, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (standard: the humanoid's own six cameras, one episode, no reset).

Simulator: robosuite @ 51cc017 (1.5.1, mink whole-body IK) / MuJoCo 3.2.6 (RoboCasa GR1 tabletop) · Edition: RoboCasa GR1 tabletop tasks @ 4840e67, all 24 (exam @ 8c5594a43) · Robots: Fourier GR1 · Adapted from an upstream benchmark

Tasks: GR1 · PnPBottleToCabinetClose; GR1 · PnPCanToDrawerClose; GR1 · PnPCupToDrawerClose; GR1 · PnPMilkToMicrowaveClose; GR1 · PnPPotatoToMicrowaveClose; GR1 · PnPWineToCabinetClose; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromCuttingboardToBasketSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromCuttingboardToCardboardboxSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromCuttingboardToPanSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromCuttingboardToPotSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromCuttingboardToTieredbasketSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromPlacematToBasketSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromPlacematToBowlSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromPlacematToPlateSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromPlacematToTieredshelfSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromPlateToBowlSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromPlateToCardboardboxSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromPlateToPanSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromPlateToPlateSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromTrayToCardboardboxSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromTrayToPlateSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromTrayToPotSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromTrayToTieredbasketSplitA; GR1 · PosttrainPnPNovelFromTrayToTieredshelfSplitA.

### MetaWorld+

All 50 of Meta-World's v3 environments for a Sawyer arm (reward v2), one frozen instance each: push, pick and place, open doors, drawers and windows, press buttons, turn dials and faucets, insert pegs, hammer, sweep and more. Each task passes or fails on Meta-World's own success checker on the state after the agent's last action, with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: full simulator state, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory of at most 500 actions handed in) and limited (standard: a robot behind a service, four fixed cameras and the arm's own state, one episode, no reset). Privileged is reported as a control; the standard mode is the benchmark.

Simulator: MuJoCo 3.3.0 (Meta-World v3) · Edition: our benchmark (exam @ 8c5594a43): Meta-World v3 @ 59fc34d, all 50 environments · Robots: Rethink Sawyer · Adapted from an upstream benchmark

Tasks: Meta-World · Assembly; Meta-World · Basketball; Meta-World · Bin picking; Meta-World · Box close; Meta-World · Button press; Meta-World · Button press topdown; Meta-World · Button press topdown wall; Meta-World · Button press wall; Meta-World · Coffee button; Meta-World · Coffee pull; Meta-World · Coffee push; Meta-World · Dial turn; Meta-World · Disassemble; Meta-World · Door close; Meta-World · Door lock; Meta-World · Door open; Meta-World · Door unlock; Meta-World · Drawer close; Meta-World · Drawer open; Meta-World · Faucet close; Meta-World · Faucet open; Meta-World · Hammer; Meta-World · Hand insert; Meta-World · Handle press; Meta-World · Handle press side; Meta-World · Handle pull; Meta-World · Handle pull side; Meta-World · Lever pull; Meta-World · Peg insert side; Meta-World · Peg unplug side; Meta-World · Pick out of hole; Meta-World · Pick place; Meta-World · Pick place wall; Meta-World · Plate slide; Meta-World · Plate slide back; Meta-World · Plate slide back side; Meta-World · Plate slide side; Meta-World · Push; Meta-World · Push back; Meta-World · Push wall; Meta-World · Reach; Meta-World · Reach wall; Meta-World · Shelf place; Meta-World · Soccer; Meta-World · Stick pull; Meta-World · Stick push; Meta-World · Sweep; Meta-World · Sweep into; Meta-World · Window close; Meta-World · Window open.

### VLABench

Language-conditioned manipulation for a Franka Panda at a table: selecting by attribute, common sense, semantic and spatial descriptions, physical question answering by pressing buttons, and multi-step tasks (heating food, setting a table, playing poker). We keep the 36 of VLABench's native tasks whose recorded expert re-verifies on a frozen instance, one instance each. Each task passes or fails on VLABench's own success checker (its termination condition), with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: every entity's pose, VLABench's skills as planning primitives, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (standard: four cameras and the arm's own state, one episode, no reset).

Simulator: MuJoCo 3.2.2 + dm_control 1.0.22 (VLABench) · Edition: VLABench @ cf588fe, our selection of 36 tasks (exam @ 8c5594a43) · Robots: Franka Panda · Adapted from an upstream benchmark

Tasks: Common sense · select_billiards_common_sense; Common sense · select_chemistry_tube_common_sense; Common sense · select_fruit_common_sense; Manipulation · add_condiment; Manipulation · book_rearrange; Manipulation · find_unseen_object; Manipulation · hammer_nail_and_hang_picture; Manipulation · heat_food; Manipulation · insert_bloom_flower; Manipulation · insert_flower; Manipulation · play_math_game; Manipulation · put_box_on_painting; Manipulation · select_billiards; Manipulation · select_chemistry_tube; Manipulation · select_drink; Manipulation · select_fruit; Manipulation · select_mahjong; Manipulation · select_nth_largest_poker; Manipulation · select_painting; Manipulation · select_poker; Manipulation · select_specific_type_book; Manipulation · select_toy; Manipulation · select_unique_type_mahjong; Manipulation · take_out_cool_drink; Manipulation · texas_holdem; Physical QA · friction_qa; Physical QA · magnetism_qa; Physical QA · reflection_qa; Semantic · select_chemistry_tube_semantic; Semantic · select_mahjong_semantic; Semantic · select_poker_semantic; Spatial · select_billiards_spatial; Spatial · select_book_spatial; Spatial · select_chemistry_tube_spatial; Spatial · select_mahjong_spatial; Spatial · select_poker_spatial.

### HumanoidBench

Whole-body tasks for a simulated Unitree H1 humanoid, bare or with two Shadow dexterous hands: locomotion (walking, stairs, hurdles, balancing, a maze, sitting) and whole-body manipulation (doors, cabinets, a bookshelf, pushing and lifting, a cube in each hand). Each episode is scored by HumanoidBench's own dense reward, summed over the episode, against its own success bar. We keep the 9 hardest of its 32 registered tasks plus one fixture, in three modes: privileged (full simulator state, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in), standard (a robot behind a service: cameras, joint readings and an IMU, 50 resets) and standard-realtime (standard on a clock that does not stop: the robot runs at 50 Hz while the agent thinks).

Simulator: MuJoCo 3 (HumanoidBench's gymnasium environments) · Edition: cb11890 (upstream), our selection of 9 tasks and a fixture (2026-10-04; 24 until then) · Robots: Unitree H1, Unitree H1 with hands · Adapted from an upstream benchmark

Tasks: Locomotion · Balance hard; Locomotion · Hurdle; Locomotion · Sit simple; Locomotion · Walk; Manipulation · Bookshelf simple; Manipulation · Cube; Manipulation · Door; Manipulation · Powerlift; Manipulation · Room; Manipulation · Window.

### MolmoSpaces

Ai2's zero-shot evaluation episodes for robot policies in unseen houses: a Franka FR3 picks, places (into a receptacle, next to an object, by colour), opens and closes fixtures, and a Rainbow RB-Y1 mobile manipulator navigates to an object and opens a room door. We keep one upstream episode per family, 8 in all: of three candidates a fixed rule picks per family (cluttered targets, upstream's Hard configurations, far and unseen navigation targets, three different houses), the hardest and most representative in the batch evaluation's runs. Each task passes or fails on upstream's own `judge_success()` at the end of the episode, with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: the simulator's full state, upstream's kinematics, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (standard: the robot's own cameras with depth and its proprioception, one episode, no reset).

Simulator: MuJoCo 3.5.0 (molmo-spaces 0.2.9) · Edition: molmo-spaces 0.2.9, benchmark molmospaces-bench-v2/20260415; our selection of 8 episodes (exam @ e46be110c, · Robots: Franka + Robotiq 2F-85, Rainbow RB-Y1 · Adapted from an upstream benchmark

Tasks: Franka · Close; Franka · Open; Franka · Pick; Franka · Pick and place; Franka · Pick and place by colour; Franka · Pick and place next to; RB-Y1 · Navigate to; RB-Y1 · Open door.

### KinDER

Physical reasoning for robot planning and control, kept apart from perception and language: a simulated TidyBot++ mobile manipulator throws, balances, sweeps, scoops, stacks into cupboards, sorts, clears and packs. Each episode passes or fails on KinDER's own goal check (an object's centre inside a goal region, and the like), with no partial credit. We keep 5 of its 31 task families (the 4 hardest, scored, and one fixture), one variant each, and run each in two modes: unlimited (full simulator state and the goal check, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (a robot behind a service: its base and wrist cameras, odometry and joint readings; one episode without resets).

Simulator: MuJoCo 3.3 (KinDER's Dynamic3D environments); PyBullet for two kinematic tasks now excluded · Edition: 5b2dbac (upstream), our selection of 4 tasks and a fixture (2026-10-04; 11 until then) · Robots: TidyBot++ · Adapted from an upstream benchmark

Tasks: Dynamic3D · Constrained cupboard; Dynamic3D · Dynamo; Dynamic3D · Sweep into drawer; Scoop Pour I01; Sweep Simple I01.

### RoboPaint

82 brush targets for a Franka Panda with a brush: Chinese calligraphy in kaishu (35) and xingshu (16), lettering (10), acrylic (10) and oil (11), each in both modes. The target has to be written or painted with strokes, the way a person does, not coloured in: writing fails when a long brush path is made of thin marks, and a painting has a path budget and its strokes must be sweeps, not zigzag, serpentine or contour-offset fills. Success needs the picture to match and the process rules to hold; work within the rules keeps a continuous score.

Simulator: ManiSkill 3.0.1 / SAPIEN 3.0.3 + brush models (calligraphy, broad nib, libmypaint 1.6.1) · Edition: ours (2026-10-05) · Robots: Franka Panda · Built for the exam

Tasks: Acrylic · Applesoranges; Acrylic · Bedroom; Acrylic · Bluehorses; Acrylic · Greatwave; Acrylic · Kajikazawa; Acrylic · Plumpark; Acrylic · Redfuji; Acrylic · Suddenshower; Acrylic · Sunflowers; Acrylic · Vision; Caoshu · Beiquelindanshui; Caoshu · Nangong; Caoshu · Siwushaonian; Caoshu · Wen; Caoshu · Zhen; Caoshu · Zhongtiangechuifen; Kaishu · Linfengguilong; Kaishu · Yongzibafa; Lettering · Aim; Lettering · Business; Lettering · Commendation; Lettering · Diligence; Lettering · Liberty; Lettering · Virtue; Oil · Bathers; Oil · Cafeterrace; Oil · Cypresses; Oil · Irises; Oil · Milkmaid; Oil · Monalisa; Oil · Pearlearring; Oil · Saintevictoire; Oil · Starrynight; Oil · Temeraire; Oil · Wanderer; Xingshu · Feng; Xingshu · He; Xingshu · Huifenghechang; Xingshu · Maolinxiuzhu; Xingshu · Nian; Xingshu · Shan; Xingshu · Xian; Xingshu · Yong.

### RoboTwin 2.0

Fifty bimanual tabletop manipulation tasks on a dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX (four other embodiments supported), each defined as one Python class: a scene builder, a success predicate and a scripted expert that RoboTwin uses to generate its public 100k-episode dataset. Domain randomisation (clutter, textures, lighting, table height) is a switch we leave off. Success is the task's own `check_success()` at the end of the episode, all-or-nothing.

Simulator: SAPIEN 3 (PhysX) + CuRobo · Edition: ICML 2026 paper (arXiv 2506.18088); code `main` @ 6dde571 (2026-09-14); assets HF revision 981c92a · Robots: ALOHA AgileX · Adapted from an upstream benchmark

Tasks: Adjust bottle; Beat block hammer; Blocks ranking rgb; Blocks ranking size; Dump bin big bin; Grab roller; Handover block; Handover microphone; Hanging mug; Lift pot; Move can pot; Move pill bottle pad; Move playing card away; Move stapler pad; Open laptop; Open microwave; Pick diverse bottles; Pick dual bottles; Place a to b left; Place a to b right; Place bread basket; Place bread skillet; Place burger fries; Place can basket; Place cans plastic box; Place container plate; Place dual shoes; Place empty cup; Place fan; Place mouse pad; Place object basket; Place object scale; Place object stand; Place phone stand; Place shoe; Press stapler; Put bottles dustbin; Rotate QR code; Scan object; Shake bottle; Shake bottle horizontally; Stack blocks three; Stack blocks two; Stack bowls three; Stack bowls two; Stamp seal; Turn switch.

### MuJoCo Playground

Thirteen environments of Google DeepMind's MuJoCo Playground, run in plain MuJoCo on the CPU. Nine are quadruped locomotion: the Unitree Go1 tracks a joystick on flat and rough ground, gets up from a fall and balances in a handstand and a footstand; Boston Dynamics Spot tracks a joystick, with and without a commanded gait, and gets up; Google's Barkour vB tracks a joystick while it is pushed. Four are manipulation: ALOHA 2 hand-over and peg insertion, and a Franka Panda that opens a cabinet and places a cube in a given orientation. Playground trains with dense rewards, so each task has a success test of ours, built from its termination rules and reward targets.

Simulator: MuJoCo 3.3.7 (plain MuJoCo on the CPU; upstream trains in MJX / MuJoCo Warp) · Edition: MuJoCo Playground (arXiv 2502.08844); code `main` @ 4057c14 · Robots: ALOHA 2, Boston Dynamics Spot, Franka Panda, Google Barkour vB, Unitree Go1 · Adapted from an upstream benchmark

Tasks: Aloha Hand Over; Aloha Single Peg Insertion; Panda Open Cabinet; Panda Pick Cube Orientation; Barkour Joystick; Go1 Footstand; Go1 Getup; Go1 Handstand; Go1 Joystick Flat Terrain; Go1 Joystick Rough Terrain; Spot Flat Terrain Joystick; Spot Getup; Spot Joystick Gait Tracking.

### DexToolBench

Twenty-four dexterous tool-use tasks from SimToolReal: 6 tool categories (hammer, marker, eraser, brush, spatula, screwdriver) x 2 real objects x 2 motions. Each task is a start pose and a sequence of goal poses for the tool, extracted from a human RGB-D demo; the score is task progress, the fraction of goals reached in order. Upstream runs it in Isaac Sim / Isaac Gym; we run SimToolReal's own MuJoCo sim2sim scene, rebuilt, with each category's table props.

Simulator: MuJoCo 3.3.7 (our port; upstream runs Isaac Sim / Isaac Gym) · Edition: SimToolReal (arXiv 2602.16863); code `main` @ 313d5ae (2026-08-13) · Robots: KUKA iiwa14 + Sharpa HA4 hand · Adapted from an upstream benchmark

Tasks: Blue brush · sweep forward; Claw hammer · swing down; Claw hammer · swing side; Flat spatula · flip over; Flat spatula · serve plate; Handle eraser · wipe c; Handle eraser · wipe smile; Long screwdriver · spin horizontal; Long screwdriver · spin vertical; Mallet hammer · swing down; Mallet hammer · swing side; Red brush · sweep forward; Red brush · sweep right; Sharpie marker · draw smile; Sharpie marker · write c; Short screwdriver · spin horizontal; Short screwdriver · spin vertical; Spoon spatula · flip over; Spoon spatula · serve plate; Staples marker · draw smile; Staples marker · write c.

### DexJoCo

The 11 tasks of DexJoCo for a 16-joint Allegro hand on a Franka Panda arm, six with one arm and five with two side by side: spray a plant, click a mouse, drive a nail, lift a bucket, pinch with tongs, fold glasses into their case, move a three-disk Hanoi tower, cook a hot dog in a microwave, unlock a tablet, fit a peg into a socket and take a photograph. Each scene is restored from a public human demonstration, success is DexJoCo's own check, and the demonstration's actions are the reference solution.

Simulator: MuJoCo 3.4 (DexJoCo's gymnasium environments, CPU) · Robots: Franka + Allegro hand, Two Franka + Allegro hands · Adapted from an upstream benchmark

Tasks: Bimanual Assembly; Bimanual Hanoi; Bimanual Microwave Cook; Bimanual Photograph; Bimanual Unlock Ipad; Click Mouse; Fold Glasses; Hammer Nail; Pick Bucket; Pinch Tongs; Water Plant.

### MyoSuite

Twenty-two MyoSuite tasks for musculoskeletal models of the human body: the MyoHand (39 muscles), the MyoArm, a table-tennis player with torso and arm, an arm next to a prosthetic arm, and the MyoLegs, one of them with a prosthetic leg. The command is one excitation per muscle, with no joint-level controller, so every reach, grasp, key turn, pen twirl, Baoding orbit, kick and run is built from muscle activations. The set spans MyoSuite's basic tasks, its MyoChallenge tasks and MyoDex object tracking.

Simulator: MyoSuite 2.12.2 (MuJoCo 3.6, CPU) · Robots: MyoArm, MyoArm + prosthetic arm, MyoArm with torso, MyoHand, MyoLeg + prosthetic leg, MyoLegs · Adapted from an upstream benchmark

Tasks: Arm Reach; Baoding; Bimanual; Chase Tag; Dex Airplane Fly; Dex Apple Lift; Dex Bunny Inspect; Dex Cup Pour; Dex Cylinder Pass; Dex Hammer Use; Die Reorient; Hand Pose; Hand Reach; Key Turn; Obj Hold; Obj Reorient; Osl Run; Pen Twirl; Relocate; Sarc Key Turn; Soccer; Table Tennis.

### RoboARC

Topological manipulation puzzles (formerly TopoGym and RoboTangle): free a coil from a cast, open interlocked claws, take a ring off a horseshoe, get a hedgehog out of its cage, pick a lock, guide a loop along a buzz wire, bundle fibers, thread and untie ropes, take rings off slotted posts, and flatten or fold a blanket. With them, IKEA furniture assembly for two arms with physical grasps: screw the legs into a LACK table, fit the dowels and panels of an EKET cabinet, drive screws into a VARIERA box with a screwdriver, close the snaps of a VESKEN shelf. ALOHA 2 or Franka Panda arms, on MuJoCo with the cloth on a deterministic GPU solver.

### RoboDojo

The simulation part of RoboDojo's benchmark for generalist manipulation policies: two ARX X5 arms with parallel grippers at a table. All 42 tasks over five capability dimensions (generalization, memory, precision, long horizon and open tasks) plus the 12 randomised variants of the generalization tasks, with other models, lighting, backgrounds and clutter. 25 continuous, multi-stage dynamic tasks for one or two Franka Panda arms with task tools (a plate, a cup, a paddle, a scoop): in every task something moves by itself, such as a tossed ball, a sliding puck, a conveyor, a pendulum or a moving cart, and the robot must catch, strike, carry, hand over, flip or release at the right moment, several times in one episode.

### BiGym 2.0

Household tasks such as a dishwasher, cupboards and drawers for a Unitree G1 with two grippers, kept balanced and walking by NVIDIA's GR00T-WBC policy. ### Embodied Olympics - Fun

Single-robot sports for a Unitree G1 or the adult-size H1-2, in their official settings: sprint, hurdles, steeplechase, high, long and triple jump, pole vault, a dunk and a layup at a 3.05 m ring, a serve over a 2.43 m net, a 7.26 kg shot put, javelin and discus, bowling, juggling, jump rope, a backflip, a giant swing on the high bar. The ball games that come at the robot (a catch, a header, a volleyball set or spike, a tennis or table-tennis return) also run in real time, where the world keeps going while the agent thinks. A referee judges from the simulator state whether the sport was done. Nothing is scaled down for the robot, most tasks have no known solution, and the agent may use the robot's walking policy, drive every joint itself, or download public controllers.

Simulator: MuJoCo 3.3.7 (CPU) · Robots: Unitree G1, Unitree H1-2 · Built for the exam

Tasks: Backflip; Badminton Serve; Balance Beam; Balance Board; Basketball Dribble; Basketball Dribble Realgrasp; Bowling; Bowling Realgrasp; Box Jump; Boxing; Catch; Catch And Shoot; Catch And Shoot Realgrasp; Catch Realgrasp; Clean And Jerk; Crawl; Discus; Discus Realgrasp; Dribble Slalom; Dunk; Dunk Between Legs; Dunk Realgrasp; Free Throw; Free Throw Realgrasp; Golf Putt; Golf Putt Realgrasp; Header; High Bar Swing; High Jump; Hurdles; Hurdles Freestanding; Javelin; Javelin Realgrasp; Juggle Three; Juggle Three Realgrasp; Juggling; Juggling Feet; Juggling Feet Realgrasp; Juggling Head; Juggling Realgrasp; Jump Rope; Kick Target; Layup; Layup Realgrasp; Long Jump; Long Rope; Paddle Bounce; Paddle Bounce Realgrasp; Penalty Kick; Pitch Target; Pitch Target Realgrasp; Pole Vault; Shot Put; Shot Put Realgrasp; Shuttle Run; Slalom; Sprint; Standing Long Jump; Steeplechase; Table Tennis Return; Table Tennis Return Realgrasp; Tennis Return; Tennis Return Realgrasp; Tennis Serve; Tennis Serve Realgrasp; Toes To Bar; Toes To Bar Realgrasp; Trap Ball; Triple Jump; Vault; Vertical Jump; Volley Shot; Volleyball Bump; Volleyball Serve; Volleyball Serve Realgrasp; Volleyball Set; Volleyball Spike; Wall Ball; Wall Ball Realgrasp.

### Embodied Olympics - Match

Whole matches against an opponent, each sport on its own service: table tennis and singles badminton with a Franka Panda and a paddle or a racket, 2 v 2 humanoid soccer with two Booster T1 robots under one program (with high-level actions, or at the joint level with no walking policy and no kick skill), 5 v 5 wheeled small-size soccer under RoboCup rules, foosball, and an épée bout for a Unitree G1. Most matches run in real time: the world never waits for the agent, slowed to a fraction of real speed and paused after each point for review; the fencing bout is turn-based on a chess clock. Opponents range from scripted players at several levels to reinforcement-learned ones, and in the low-level variants the agent builds the core stroke itself from the robot's joint interface.

Simulator: MuJoCo 3.3.7 (CPU), each sport on its own match service · Robots: Booster T1, Foosball rods, Franka Panda, RoboCup Small Size robots, Unitree G1 · Built for the exam

Tasks: Badminton Duelrl I01; Badminton Match I01; Badminton Match I02; Badminton Match I04; Badminton Matchlow I01; Fencing Bout I01; Fencing Bout I02; Foosball Match I01; Soccer Jointcpu I01; Soccer Jointgpu I01; Soccer Match; Soccerssl Match; Soccerssl Match I01; Tabletennis Duelrl I01; Tabletennis Match I01; Tabletennis Match I02; Tabletennis Match I03; Tabletennis Match I04; Tabletennis Matchlow I01.

### Embodied Safety Exam

Safety for an agent that operates a robot for a person. Every family pairs requests whose literal execution ends in harm (an injury, a fire, poison, a shock, something broken) with harmless twins of the same kind. The verdict comes from what physically happened in the simulation, read by written hazard rules, and from how the episode ended, never from the agent's text. A UR5e, a Franka FR3, two YAM arms and a TidyBot++, with low-level control; standard mode, plus a real-time set.

### DexHandExam

Ten dexterous-hand tasks, one frozen scene each: six with a Sharpa Wave hand on a wrist stage (cube layers, a held joystick, a pen regrasp, two objects, a rotary gait, a cube reorientation), assembling a hamburger, folding paper in half, and two with a hand on each of two Tianji Marvin arms (sweeping into a dustpan, moving a pot to a shelf). No assisted grasp: objects move only through contact and gravity. Every task also runs with a Wuji hand.

Simulator: MuJoCo 3.4.0 (CPU) · Robots: Two Tianji Marvin arms with Sharpa Wave hands, Sharpa Wave hand on a wrist stage, Two Sharpa Wave hands on wrist stages · Built for the exam

Tasks: Assemble Hamburger; Batter Whisk; Bicycle Pump Stroke; Binder Page Load; Book Page Turn; Boot Sole Brush; Coffee Stir; Drying Rack Unfold; Envelope Letter Insert; Essential Cube Layer; Essential Cube Reorient; Essential Held Joystick; Essential Pen Regrasp; Essential Rotary Gait; Essential Two Object; Fan Guard Install; Grinder Crank; Jar Lid Open; Pancake Serve; Paper Half Fold; Paper Staple; Picture Hang; Pot Shelf Transfer; Ram Module Install; Remote Battery Swap; Stool Brace Insert; Sweep Dustpan; Tray Glass Carry; Usb Plug Insert; Vacuum Bin Reseat.

### iSpatialGym

Spatial intelligence on a mobile two-armed robot in house-scale scenes. Each task gives only a goal image, the head camera's view once the task is done, and the robot has to make the scene match it: an object's pose, a relation between two objects, an articulation, or its own viewpoint. No sentence names the objects.

Simulator: OmniGibson (BEHAVIOR-1K fork) on Isaac Sim 5.1 · Robots: Galaxea R1 Pro · Built for the exam

Tasks: Alignment Axial; Alignment Vertical; Camera Relocalization Obstructed; Configuration Matching Articulation Open Small Scale; Configuration Matching Block Design; Inter Object Relation Satisfaction Inside Small Scale; Inter Object Relation Satisfaction Nextto Small Scale; Inter Object Relation Satisfaction Ontop Small Scale; Inter Object Relation Satisfaction Touching Small Scale; Inter Object Relation Satisfaction Under Small Scale; Mental Rotation; Object Scaling.

### RoboWits

30 seed tabletop tasks for a fixed bimanual robot, each requiring a physical insight rather than a longer motion: use a ruler to align, a dustpan to sweep, a funnel to pour, an inclined plane to move a box. 163 published mutations vary the scene while keeping the parent task's success predicate. Scored by the task's own success checker.

Simulator: Genesis 0.4.7 (gs_gym) · Edition: code release 2026-06-04 (commit 9cc30ae) · Robots: Marvin · Adapted from an upstream benchmark

Tasks: Align Blocks; Ball Into Bottle; Ball Onto Tower; Collect Screws; Cover With Lid; Dominos; Gap Retrieve; Hold Cup; Move Cube; Raise Platform; Retrieve Cube; Stack Bowls; Stack Cubes; Stand Bulb; Stand Pages.

### ManiGuard

A manipulation safety benchmark from the NU IDEAS Lab: tabletop tasks for a Franka Panda with long fin-ray fingers, each with a safety specification in linear temporal logic over physics predicates (dropped, upright, on top of, closed, touching), checked after every control step. A task counts only if the goal holds and no rule was ever broken.

Simulator: BEHAVIOR-1K v3.7.2 (OmniGibson 3.7.2 on Isaac Sim 4.5) · Robots: Franka Panda · Adapted from an upstream benchmark

Tasks: Cabinet Pickup I19; Cabinet Pickup I20; Cabinet Pickup I22; Cabinet Pickup I26; Cabinet Pickup I29; Clutter Pickup I09; Clutter Pickup I15; Clutter Pickup I23; Clutter Pickup I25; Clutter Pickup I28; Dusty Transfer I03; Dusty Transfer I16; Dusty Transfer I20; Dusty Transfer I24; Dusty Transfer I25; Jar Transport I02; Jar Transport I09; Jar Transport I13; Jar Transport I14; Jar Transport I25; Lid Transport I06; Lid Transport I07; Lid Transport I12; Lid Transport I15; Lid Transport I16; Stack Retrieve I08; Stack Retrieve I10; Stack Retrieve I12; Stack Retrieve I13; Stack Retrieve I21.

### RoboEngineer

RoboEngineer recreates the iteration loop of real-world sim2real robot engineering in simulation. A coding agent develops a controller or policy in a public nominal simulator, then deploys it to a separate simulator with hidden dynamics that differ from its training environment. Using only deployment video and noisy telemetry as feedback, it diagnoses failures and refines its controller or training pipeline over at most three adaptation rounds. The selected policy is evaluated on held-out episodes of the same hidden plant, testing whether improvements transfer beyond the observed trials. Thirty tasks span fifteen families and two hidden plants per family: quadrotor landing and flight in wind, racing-car tracking, drifting and lapping, Go2 quadruped attitude control, jumping and weaving, and G1 humanoid walking over terrain.

Simulator: MuJoCo and learned dynamics surrogates (quadrotors, a racing car, Unitree Go2 and G1) · Robots: AnyCar racing car, Intel Aero quadrotor, Neural-Fly quadrotor, Unitree G1, Unitree Go2 · Built for the exam

Tasks: Anycar Compact Lap Monaco 6; Anycar Compact Lap Monaco 6 I01; Anycar Compact Lap Silverstone 8; Anycar Compact Lap Silverstone 8 I01; Anycar Drift Park; Anycar Drift Park I01; Anycar Tight Drift Park; Anycar Tight Drift Park I01; Anycar Tracking; Anycar Tracking I01; G1 Terrain Walk; G1 Terrain Walk I01; Go2 Attitude; Go2 Attitude I01; Go2 Forward Jump; Go2 Forward Jump I01; Go2 Weave; Go2 Weave I01; Go2 Yaw Jump; Go2 Yaw Jump I01; Landing Random Pad; Landing Random Pad I01; Neuralfly Eight; Neuralfly Eight I01; Neuralfly General; Neuralfly General I01; Neuralfly General Skydio; Neuralfly General Skydio I01; Neuralfly Vector Wind; Neuralfly Vector Wind I01.
